author: Avery Boyce
title: Northport daycare announces closure during child abuse investigation - NewsBreak
text:
By Avery Boyce ,
5 hours ago
NORTHPORT, Ala. ( WIAT ) — The Word Academy announced it will close its daycare less than a week into an investigation involving alleged child abuse.
The daycare is located off of Highway 69 North in Northport. The child-care facility is a part of the Word Community Church.
On Friday, the Department of Human Resources gave India Keller a call she never expected to receive.
“I can’t even say what was going through my mind,” Keller said. “I was just worried about getting to him, getting him out and away from there.”
Keller enrolled her 10-month-old son at Word Academy in August. DHR notified Keller that the state agency was at the daycare checking on her son, who was involved in alleged abuse that happened at Word Academy.
“I now know why he is acting the way he is,” Keller said. “I know why he’s terrified to be laid down now. He’s traumatized.”
Over the last month, Keller noticed minor bruises on her child’s face. Until DHR called, marks never raised any alarms. Now, she continues to seek answers from the daycare and church.
“They’ve met me with 100% certainty that it was untrue,” Keller said.
Jeffrey Smith, the attorney representing Word Academy, sent CBS 42 a statement. It reads in part:
“The leadership of the Academy as well as the Church recently became aware of allegations of abuse involving a staff member of The Academy. We take these matters with the utmost seriousness. Immediately upon learning of the allegations, we placed the employee in question on administrative leave while we initiated both an internal review and cooperation with law enforcement. During the course of the investigation, additional information came to light that warranted the immediate termination of this employee. In addition, after careful consideration, we have made the decision to terminate the Director.”
Auburn University president terminates employees over “hurtful and insensitive” social media posts Word Community Church decided Wednesday it would close the day care. Teachers were told mid-afternoon, and parents were supposed to be notified as they picked up their child Wednesday, according to Smith.
The Alabama Department of Human Resouces requested the Tuscaloosa County Sheriffs Office’s assistance in the case earlier this week, TCSO Sgt. Josh Hastings said.
“No arrests at this point,” Hastings said. “We’re in the early stages of this investigation, which is based on the allegations originally reported to DHR.”
The church and day care are cooperating with law enforcement, according to the TCSO and Word Academy’s attorney.
Meanwhile, Keller is still without answers as to what exactly happened to her son.
” It’s very disheartening,” Keller said. “I waited until he was older to put him in school because I was terrified of this. Be the helicopter parent, ask the questions.”
